references.text: The preceding verse describes the burning bush that Moses sees, which is the basis for his curiosity in verse 3.
Moses refers to 'the one who lived in the thornbush' (הַסְּנֶה), pointing back to this revelation at the burning bush.
God responds to Moses' decision to approach the bush and calls out to him from the thornbush.
Stephen's speech in Acts refers to this event where Moses saw the vision (τὸ ὅραμα) and approached to look more closely.
Jesus refers to the thornbush (ἐπὶ τῆς βάτου) as proof of the resurrection, pointing to this revelation to Moses.
Jesus mentions 'the book of Moses, in the passage about the thornbush' (ἐπὶ τοῦ βάτου) as testimony to God's promise.
A direct allusion where the New Testament confirms that the angel in the thornbush was the source of Moses' authority as leader and deliverer.
